name: cfcmt-bus-source-compression-ablation-v1
terminal_sampling_change: All 240 terminal rows retained in both pools; their uniform-sampling proportion changes from 240/16384 to 240/3284718. Expected terminal draws over 50000*256 samples change from 187500 to about 935.
fixed_settings: Same trainer_config, architecture, reward_scale, IQL update order, seed, minibatch size and logging interval as the completed pilot source initialization. Arrival-rate inputs omitted as before. Original transition pairs retained.
snapshot: Before training, compare all consumed compact-source rows fieldwise against the original history after rate omission, then copy the complete history into an independent CFCMT-owned H5 in bounded chunks. Training reads only this copy and existing CFCMT frozen runtime.
reference: Existing fixed-final sparse source initializers; do not retrain or select them.
diagnostic_states: Same 256 source positions from the consumed compact pool, all 240 source terminal tails, and all 2048 target stop plus 2048 target calibrate rows. Native and exact column-reset transfer stages; no target adaptation.
primary_diagnostics: Recorded-action minimum-head Q and positive fraction, V/current/next extremes, IQL residual MAE, terminal anchors; report all three seeds against sparse initializers.
checkpoint_rule: Fixed final 50000-update initializer, no diagnostic-based checkpoint selection.
admission: Load complete frozen source replay and run 3 updates only to verify memory, native sampling and finite training metrics; separate fresh learner for every formal seed.
interpretation: Source available data quantity and sampling density change together; equal update counts are not equal source sample budgets. This isolates the prior source compression decision, not sparse support versus terminal weighting individually. Value recovery is not a closed-loop performance result.
next_decision: Assess whether full source history reduces the existing positive-value and catastrophic-next-value errors before another target adaptation or continuation experiment. Keep all negative seeds and the previous pilot results.
